brief.ask: Create a brand identity for Portwise, the freight visibility platform in this folder.
brief.owner: Owner preferences: dependable and calm, for operations teams who look at it all day; serious enough for enterprise procurement. No globes, ships, containers, trucks or arrows. Web app, sales decks and LinkedIn.

claim.notes: Only Porta cleared the gate (blind avg 6.4); finalized with insufficient-evidence originality accepted, and the name Portwise has a likely unverified trademark conflict (Portwise B.V., classes 35/39/42) that needs a lawyer before any use.

concepts.title: Confidence Band
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s6 a notification-bell UI icon (dome over base line), second read a chart bell curve, so a UI icon plus the product's own object drawn plainly; s7 a traffic cone at first glance, which signals construction or hazard, the opposite of calm and dependable; s8 a letter A, then a tombstone or arch window: a different letter plus a grim misreading. All three struck. Lesson: once the bell curve is closed into a solid dome it turns into a bell, cone or arch. If this direction comes back, the confidence range must not be drawn as a filled distribution silhouette. Try it as an interval instead: a held span between two precise end marks, with no peak and no dome.

concepts.title: Interval
readsAs: a letter H with its crossbar floating loose (or a sideways I-beam)
a bracketed minus / collapse toggle [-] or a UI range-slider handle
a brick or dumbbell between two posts. Most unfortunate for ops teams: a 'minus / remove / collapsed' UI control
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a monoline lowercase p with a dot, also a hook or an eye; s2 a cursive P / question mark with a ball end, generic script; s3 a route on a map ending at a destination dot (the route-line cliché the brief bans, struck); s4 a square-cornered P, Greek-key / ruled spiral, ending on one dot. Pick s4: most precise and gridded (fits calm/precise/enterprise), best at 16 px (0.95), and the inward square wind is the only one with ownable geometry. Risks: a line ending on a round dot still reads as a route/GPS destination - consider ending the line on a square terminal or a dot that sits in a gap rather than on the stroke (tool also warns thread and dot merge in one colour - add a gap); a square spiral P risks a parking sign or a generic pixel-font P; the spiral needs one more deliberate turn or proportion so it reads as a wound timeline, not just a P outline.

concepts.title: Porta
readsAs: a round-topped doorway split down the middle
two mirrored stepped Art Deco towers (skyline, real-estate developer)
a ziggurat or mirrored bar chart. Unfortunate: a pair of headstones / twin towers, or a property-developer logo
concepts.sketchNotes: Reads as: s1 a lowercase n / arch doorway (different letter, struck); s2 a stepped arched window or brick gate tower, no letter, no UI icon; s3 a lowercase h / n with a cut and dropped half (initial-with-cut device plus wrong letter, struck); s4 a bold stock P with a rounded counter, barely distinguishable from any heavy sans P (weak, low ownability). Pick s2: the only one that is a shape before it is a letter, and the stacked stages give the timeline idea a body. Risks: reads as a building/castle/Lego stack or stained-glass window; the tiny top tier looks fussy and will clog at 16 px (0.88); three bands with a slot drift toward a brick wall. Develop: fewer, calmer parts (two or three tiers with generous, consistent gaps), make the central slot clearly the through-line from ground to crown, check the round crown does not become a tombstone, and keep it plum, flat, one colour.
